statement: Base operating point: minion clock 600 MHz at 0.517 V on die (median while a kernel runs, aifoundry2). A warm card is held here by the governor; every table in the reports is at this point.
note: Minion rail voltage at 600 MHz by card: 518 mV (aifoundry2), 522-523 mV (aifoundry3), 499 mV (aifoundry1-c1) (manual.json catalogue.rail_mv; 01-at-rest.md "The three cards").

statement: Second operating point: 700 MHz at 0.568 V, reached only from a cool start on aifoundry2 (V^2 f: 1.41x the 600 MHz switching power).
note: aifoundry3 never leaves 600 MHz (TDP 0 W set by a boot service); aifoundry1-c1 sat at 600 MHz in every sample of the version-3 check.
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: Top operating point: 800 MHz at 0.618 V, reached only below about 68 C die on aifoundry2 (V^2 f: 1.91x the 600 MHz switching power).
note: The 0.52 / 0.57 / 0.62 V shorthand in the text rounds 0.517 / 0.568 / 0.618.
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: Peak board power at 800 MHz on random data: 87.8 W, for an instant before the governor stepped down (cold start).
note: E10, DATA/vf.json randn800_peak.
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: On a cool die (62-63 C) a zeros matmul reached 11.38 and 11.81 TFLOPS, spending 5-6 s of a 7 s run at 800 MHz; random data only 9.29-9.33 TFLOPS (under 0.3 s at 800 MHz).
note: The data sets the power, and the power the clock: about a 25% speed gap zeros vs random (E10).

statement: The mesh network-on-chip runs at 400 MHz; minion clock 600 MHz; LPDDR4X at a 933 MHz DDR clock (3,733 MT/s).
source: docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html header ("minion clock 600 MHz, NoC 400 MHz, LPDDR4X at 3,733 MT/s"); ridge-data noc_mhz 400
note: The 933 MHz DDR clock is read from card telemetry / SP firmware mem_controller.c (ridge-data levels[dram].spec.src); 3,733 MT/s assumes the 1066:4266 ratio.

statement: Mesh (NoC) rail at 484-486 mV on die, the same on all three cards (0.485 V is the voltage Heat per millimetre scales from).
source: manual.json: catalogue.rail_mv.<card>.noc (a2 484, a3 484, a1c1 486); docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/report.json inputs (noc 0.485 V)

statement: SRAM rail (L2, L3, scratchpad arrays) at 704 mV on aifoundry2, 698 mV on aifoundry3, 751 mV on aifoundry1-c1.
note: By V^2 alone aifoundry1-c1 SRAM accesses would cost 14% more (08-cards.md).

statement: L1 data cache hit: 5.25 cycles load-to-use (8.8 ns at 600 MHz); the same on three cards (per-pass ranges 5.247-5.259).
note: Only 512 B of L1 per hart: the firmware puts the L1 in scratchpad mode before every launch.

statement: L2 read buffer (8 clean lines per bank x 4 banks = 2 KB per shire): 36 cycles (60 ns), 11 fewer than the L2 array.
note: Spec: 10 vs 21 shire cycles (CORE-ET Shire Cache Specification), per the memory-hierarchy page.

statement: L2 cache hit (and the shire's own scratchpad): 47 cycles (78 ns); hart 1 pays 3 more (39 read buffer, 50 L2).
note: The single-load ladder of Anatomy reads L2 at 49 cycles in every pass (a different probe and offset).

statement: The shire's own L2 scratchpad: 47 cycles (78 ns), the same SRAM, latency and bandwidth as the L2 cache.
note: Re-measured on three cards 26 Sep (E36).

statement: Another shire's scratchpad: 99.84 + 12.00 cycles per mesh hop at 600 MHz (112-220 cycles, 186-366 ns over 1-10 hops); all 124 points within 1 cycle, a->b equals b->a within 0.032 cycles.
note: Clock model (aifoundry2, 18 Sep): 66 minion cycles + 56 ns + 20 ns per hop.

statement: L3 hit against distance to the line's home shire: 110.5 + 11.99 cycles per mesh hop (from shire 0), within 4 cycles for 99.4-100% of lines on each card.
note: A local L3 hit is ~110 cycles: ~48 for the L1 and L2 lookup and miss, ~62 for the home slice (Anatomy, inferred). 31 of 32 L3 lines live in another shire.

statement: L3 hit from a pointer chase, averaged over all 32 slices: 159-169 cycles at 600 MHz (265-282 ns), by requesting shire: 168.8-168.9 (shire 0), 160.6-160.7 (7), 159.1-159.2 (24), 168.8-168.9 (31).
note: The value field is the fastest requester (shire 24). Clock model: 72 cycles + 61 ns + 20 ns per hop.

statement: DRAM load from a pointer chase: 287-297 cycles at 600 MHz (479-495 ns): 296.6-297.1 from shires 0 and 31, 287.2-288.8 from 7 and 24; about 490 ns, a fifth more than an A100's HBM (405 ns).
note: The value field is the slowest requesters (shires 0 and 31). At 800 MHz (aifoundry2 only) 352-368 cycles, 440-460 ns: the mesh and DDR parts do not scale with the minion clock.

statement: A typical DRAM load, timed one at a time: 299 cycles (500 ns), the median of 4,500 loads from shire 0 to random lines; 299 in each of 15 passes on three cards.
DRAM latency model: 110 + 12 x hops(requester -> L3 home) + 91 + 12 x hops(L3 home -> memory shire) cycles; within 3 cycles for 97% (a2), 93% (a3), 94% (a1c1) of lines, left as fitted on 19 Sep.
note: Fitted on aifoundry2 (one constant plus eight memory-shire positions); PA bits 10:6 pick the L3 home, bits 8:6 the memory shire.

statement: Of a DRAM load's ~300 cycles only about 25-28 are the DRAM chip's own timing (activate tRCD 18 ns, 19.3 ns read latency, one or two 4.3 ns bursts); the rest is paths on the chip.
source: docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html section 4 ("Of the 91 cycles (152 ns), the DRAM chip itself accounts for about 25-28")
note: From the controller's timing registers set against the fit; the memory shire (queue, PHY, clock crossings) is at most ~63-66 cycles.

statement: LPDDR4X refresh every 2,325 cycles (3.88 us) on every card; a load that meets it waits up to 208 extra cycles (347 ns).
Two loads to the same bank but different rows, issued together: the second pays about +37 cycles (a2 36.9, a3 37.4, a1c1 36.5); bank = PA[12:10].
No cache level wakes up slower after idle: no shift of 5 cycles or more at any level after 16M idle cycles, on every card (no array power gating seen).
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: L1 hits, 32 B vector loads by both harts: 14.5 TB/s chip-wide (23.6 B per minion-cycle) in the energy manual's unrolled loop; the memory-hierarchy probe's loop reaches 6.2 TB/s (10 B per minion-cycle). Spec: 32 B per cycle.
source: docs/reports/2026-09-18-et-soc1-ridge-points.html ridge-data: levels[l1d].demonstrated (bpc 23.57, gbps 14,480; by card 14,474-14,488), .measured (bpc 10.04, gbps_600 6,211), .spec.bpc 32
note: The 6.2 TB/s figure is aifoundry2 and aifoundry3 (rerun passes); the 14.5 TB/s catalogue figure is on all three cards.

statement: L2 cache, 1 KB tensor loads by every minion: 2.45 TB/s chip-wide, 4.0 B per minion-cycle (128 B per shire-cycle), half the four banks' 256 B per shire-cycle spec.
note: A lone minion reads 6.4 B per cycle from L2 or scratchpad on all three cards (ridge points, three-card check).

statement: Own-shire scratchpad: 2.46 TB/s chip-wide, 4.0 B per minion-cycle, same as the L2. Tensor stores into it reach 1.23 TB/s (half the read rate).
source: ridge-data: levels[scp].measured (bpc 4.000, gbps 2,456); limits.write_gbps.tstore_scp (1,230 on each card)
note: Read rate on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3 (rerun passes); the store rate on all three cards.

statement: L3, every minion streaming: 0.98 TB/s chip-wide, 1.6 B per minion-cycle; spec (assumed one 64 B beat per NoC cycle per shire port) 3.3 TB/s, 5.33 B per minion-cycle.
Another shire's scratchpad (each shire reading the one 16 IDs away, 2.1 hops on average): 0.96 TB/s chip-wide, 1.56 B per minion-cycle.
note: If many shires read one shire's scratchpad its four mesh ports would allow only about 0.1 TB/s (ridge points, inferred).

statement: DRAM streaming: 76 GB/s for the whole chip (0.124 B per minion-cycle), about 64% of the 119 GB/s that 16 x 16-bit channels carry at 3,733 MT/s; about a twentieth of an A100.
source: ridge-data: levels[dram].measured (bpc 0.1235, gbps 75.9), .spec (gbps 119.5; datasheet max 136.5); docs/findings/05-claims.md:370
note: Tensor stores to DRAM also 76 GB/s on all three cards; stores through the L1 only 27 GB/s (ridge-data limits.write_gbps). The runtime's 128,000 MB/s is a firmware placeholder constant.

statement: A lone minion streams 1.4 B per cycle from DRAM, so at least about 93 minions streaming 1 KB loads at once are needed to reach the chip's 76 GB/s.
note: The lone-minion DRAM rate depends on the kernel (0.91 B/cycle in the catalogue loop: at least ~140 minions).

statement: Host link: PCIe Gen4 x8, 15.75 GB/s per direction before protocol overhead; host transfers have not been timed on these cards.
note: Never measured (05-claims ridge row kind A).

statement: TensorSend on the neighbourhood fast local network (pairs on tree edges), every minion sending 1 KB messages: 2,992 GB/s chip-wide, 4.9 B per minion-cycle.
note: Rates are one session on aifoundry2 (18 Sep); the energies below are three cards.

statement: TensorSend around rings of 8 or 32 minions inside a shire: 1,120 GB/s chip-wide (1.8 B per minion-cycle).
TensorSend between shires: 87-156 GB/s chip-wide over six shire-to-shire ring patterns (0.25 B per minion-cycle at best): 7-34x less message bandwidth than inside a shire.
note: Limited by how many packets a sender keeps in flight (3-5 GB/s per shire).

statement: One TensorSend link, 1 KB messages: 5.3 GB/s on the fast local network, 2.9 through the shire crossbar, 2.7 over one mesh hop, 1.8 over 10 hops (the three cards agree to the digits).
L1 hit (memhier loop): 0.75 pJ/B [0.62-0.88] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 0.77, a3 0.75, a1c1 0.72.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json: reruns.levels_pj_per_byte["l1"] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table 4.2
note: The manual recommends the catalogue's L1 row instead: flw.ps 0.54 pJ/B [0.52-0.56] random, 0.39 zeros (4.1). Brackets are the range over 18 passes (6 per card).

statement: L2 cache: 3.11 pJ/B [1.42-4.99] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 2.64, a3 2.83, a1c1 3.86.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json: reruns.levels_pj_per_byte["l2"] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table 4.2
note: Contents not set; moves a lot pass to pass (1.42-4.99).

statement: L3 (over the mesh): 14.7 pJ/B [7.1-20.5] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 12.3, a3 13.5, a1c1 18.4.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json: reruns.levels_pj_per_byte["l3"] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table 4.2
note: Contents not set; 7.1-20.5 pJ/B pass to pass.

statement: DRAM: 114.6 pJ/B [89.0-141.3] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 111.5, a3 105.6, a1c1 126.6.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json: reruns.levels_pj_per_byte["dram"] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table 4.2
note: About 70% of a DRAM byte's energy lands on no metered rail (DDR PHY, I/O, the DRAM chips); the E30 fit puts ~73 pJ/B of it off-rail.

statement: Own scratchpad filled with zeros: 2.25 pJ/B [2.06-2.61] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 2.11, a3 2.10, a1c1 2.55.
Own scratchpad filled with random data: 4.40 pJ/B [3.94-5.08] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 4.13, a3 4.04, a1c1 5.03.
note: The only level where cards differ beyond noise: aifoundry1-c1 reads above the registered band (5.03 vs 3.7-4.7).

statement: Scratchpad 16 shire IDs away (2.1 hops mean) filled with zeros: 5.10 pJ/B [4.40-6.45] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 5.04, a3 4.55, a1c1 5.71.

Scratchpad 16 shire IDs away (2.1 hops mean) filled with random data: 11.8 pJ/B [9.5-14.4] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 11.1, a3 10.8, a1c1 13.6.
Tensor load from DRAM (catalogue, both data sets): 94.6 pJ/B [86.2-105.7] on zeros, 132.6 [117.9-145.4] on random data; tensor store to DRAM 94.4 / 141.9. Even DRAM is data-dependent.
note: Per card, random: a2 134.8, a3 127.3, a1c1 135.8 pJ/B.

statement: Stores to DRAM through the L1 write-back path (fsw.ps): 341.5 pJ/B [317.4-373.3] on random data, 2.4x a tensor store, at 27 GB/s: each store allocates its line, so the byte pays a read and a write.
Tensor load from the own scratchpad (catalogue): 2.12 pJ/B on zeros, 4.43 on random data; tensor store into it 4.65 / 8.58: a scratchpad write is twice a read.
L1 hit, flw.ps 32 B by both harts: 0.54 pJ/B [0.52-0.56] on random data, 0.39 on zeros, including the instruction: an L1 hit is nearly free.
DRAM is 30x the energy of the shire's own scratchpad per byte read, and 17x per byte written.
note: Ratio of the catalogue rows above (random data).

statement: Filling one 64 B line from the scratchpad into the L1: 101 pJ on zeros, 238 pJ on random data (1.6 and 3.7 pJ per byte of line).
note: Difference of catalogue strides (stride64 - stride32) x 2; per card random a2 221, a3 223, a1c1 271 pJ.

statement: Integer add: 6.2 pJ [5.6-6.9] on zeros, 9.7 [9.3-10.3] on random operands, both harts of 1,024 minions flat out (little more than a nop, 5.1 pJ).
Scalar float add fadd.s: 23.7 pJ [22.0-24.5] on zeros, 26.3 [24.1-27.0] on random data: 3.8x an integer add even on zeros (the FPU does not gate on zero).
8-lane vector multiply-add fmadd.ps: 27.1 pJ [26.4-28.9] on zeros, 55.8 [53.8-57.0] on random data, 7.0 pJ per lane-MAC (6.3-6.4 with the instruction issue taken out); 16 flops.
note: Per card random: a2 55.6, a3 56.2, a1c1 55.4. The vector lane is ~10% above the tensor unit's 5.8 pJ per multiply-add.

statement: 8-lane vector add fadd.ps: 22.4 pJ on zeros (same as the scalar op: lanes on zeros add nothing), 41.1 on random data (5.1 per lane).
Transcendental fexp.ps (8 lanes): 155.4 pJ [147.3-162.4] on random data at a quarter the issue rate; flog.ps 218 pJ. No hardware divide or square root: they trap.
The awake core's issue floor: a nop costs 5.1 pJ [4.8-5.7] and a fence 4.4 [4.0-4.8] per instruction with both harts.
An awake minion (addi loop) costs about 2 mW (1.87 mW one hart, 3.02 mW both harts, aifoundry2); 5.1 / 6.6 pJ per instruction pooled over three cards.
note: Keeping 1,024 minions awake for a second is 2-3.1 J, against 36 J for the card at 80 C.

statement: A minion stalled on a contended atomic draws about 1.2 mW (1,024 stalled: 1.19 W [1.01-1.41] over idle), less than a spinning one (1.9 mW): waiting is cheap.
Cheapest and dearest instruction in the 161 that execute in U-mode: fence 4.6 pJ, amoaddg.d 1,486 pJ (aifoundry2, 23 Sep catalogue); atomics span 351-1,450 pJ in the three-card catalogue.
note: The 1,486 figure is the 23 Sep edition on aifoundry2; the three-card manual text gives the 351-1,450 range.

statement: TensorFMA fp32 random: 5.782 pJ per multiply-add [5.347-6.133] above idle, all 1,024 minions; per card a2 5.920, a3 5.369, a1c1 6.058.
source: manual.json: tensor.bars.fp32_randn (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/03-instructions.md:45
note: Loaded (idle included, aifoundry2 at 80 C): 13.84 pJ per MAC. 546 cycles per 16x16x16 op. Launched at 80 C (a3 at 57 C); amendment C2 offset applies.

statement: TensorFMA fp32 zeros: 0.273 pJ per multiply-add [0.141-0.445] above idle, all 1,024 minions; per card a2 0.403, a3 0.163, a1c1 0.251.
source: manual.json: tensor.bars.fp32_zeros (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/03-instructions.md:43
note: Zeros clock nothing: the lane clock is withheld when an operand word is zero.

statement: TensorFMA fp16 random: 2.590 pJ per multiply-add [2.397-2.730] above idle, all 1,024 minions; per card a2 2.661, a3 2.410, a1c1 2.700.
source: manual.json: tensor.bars.fp16_randn (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/03-instructions.md:48

statement: TensorFMA int8 random: 0.295 pJ per multiply-add [0.260-0.317] above idle, all 1,024 minions; per card a2 0.313, a3 0.262, a1c1 0.309.
source: manual.json: tensor.bars.int8_randn (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/03-instructions.md:51
note: int8 is about 19x cheaper per MAC than fp32 (E38: 18.9-20.5 by card). 318 cycles per 16x16x64 op.

statement: Dense fp32 matmul per FLOP: 6.9 pJ loaded (63.6 W over 9.18 TFLOP/s, aifoundry2 at 80 C) and 2.89 pJ marginal [2.67-3.07 over runs and cards].

Tensor unit energy by RTL event (fitted on aifoundry2): 3.18 fJ per register bit clocked, 0.025 per multiplier-tree net toggle, 0.80 per other net toggle, 15.5 per operand-word bit; 1.8 mW per minion of state machines. A random tile prices at 27.2 W on 1,024 minions.
note: A fit (E17); 14 structured matrices predicted to 0.9 W rms before they ran.

statement: Tensor matmul, tiles in L2, all 1,024 minions at 600 MHz: 9.51 TFLOP/s fp32, 19.02 fp16, 71.77 TOP/s int8, the same on each card (91-97% of the 9.83 / 19.66 / 78.6 peak); 529 cycles per fp32/fp16 op, 280.35 per int8 op.
note: Every result bit-exact against a host reference.

statement: Tensor peak per minion-cycle: 16 fp32 / 32 fp16 / 128 int8 ops; 9.83 TFLOP/s, 19.7 TFLOP/s and 78.6 TOP/s on 1,024 minions at 600 MHz.
note: Minion VPU Specification sec. 2.

statement: aifoundry2: board power under the fp32 tensor matmul (tiles in L2) 59.0 W against 33.3 W idle just before (die 80 C); 25.7 W above idle. int8: 61.2 W; fp32 from DRAM: 42.4 W.
note: Four passes; the matmul page's three-card table.

statement: aifoundry3: board power under the fp32 tensor matmul (tiles in L2) 50.4 W against 26.0 W idle just before (die 62 C); 24.4 W above idle. int8: 52.1 W; fp32 from DRAM: 34.4 W.
note: Four passes; the matmul page's three-card table.

statement: aifoundry1-c1: board power under the fp32 tensor matmul (tiles in L2) 69.1 W against 41.8 W idle just before (die 75 C); 27.2 W above idle. int8: 74.9 W; fp32 from DRAM: 50.6 W.
note: Four passes; the matmul page's three-card table.

statement: Board GFLOP/s per W, L2 matmul fp32 / fp16 / int8: aifoundry2 161 / 316 / 1,172; aifoundry3 189 / 370 / 1,377; aifoundry1-c1 138 / 270 / 958 (each card at its own die temperature).
note: Against the A100 spec sheet (peak / TDP) at full fp32 precision the card is 3.3x (a2), 3.9x (a3), 2.8x (a1c1) more energy-efficient on the benchmark's +-1/+-2 operands; the A100's int8 tensor cores lead by 1.13-1.63x.

statement: The same fp32 TensorFMA draws 38 W on zeros, 47 on ones and 64 on random-normal values on aifoundry2 at 80 C; 51 / 60 / 78 W on aifoundry1-c1 at 80 C (idle 50 W); 27 / 35 / 50 W on aifoundry3 at 57-58 C: the data decides the dynamic power.
note: Board = the idle bracket plus the measured over-idle power, four runs per card (version-3 ablation); amendment C2 launch-temperature offset.

statement: At full load only zeros hold a steady temperature: random-normal data takes the die from 80 to 90 C in 19-26 s (four runs), ones in 107-167 s; zeros cool it to 76-78 C over 10 minutes.
Idle law (aifoundry2): P_idle(T) = 12.6 W + 23.3 W x e^((T - 80 C)/36 C): 35.9 W at 80 C, rising 0.65 W per degree there; predicted the idle 20.6 h later to +0.01 W.
source: manual.json: rest.P_fix_w 12.63, A_leak_80_w 23.26, T_L_c 36, lambda_80_w_per_c 0.646; docs/energy-manual/01-at-rest.md:9
note: A fit (E17); only the total and the slope are pinned down.

statement: Leakage at 80 C is 20-29 W of the 35.9 W idle (fixed part 7-16 W): the idle bins fit equally well with the leakage e-folding anywhere from 30 to 45 C.
Leakage share at 80 C (best-fit law): 65% of an idle card (64% of the 36.3 W measured) and 36% of a card running a random-data fp32 matmul; above the 5-30% called typical for a mature chip.
note: Busy leakage share not identified in the version-3 check (0.17-0.80 fit equally well; E44).
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: Idle board power per card at 80 C by each card's own law: 35.9 W (aifoundry2), 37.3 W (aifoundry3), 48.9 W (aifoundry1-c1); aifoundry3 idles +1.01 W and aifoundry1-c1 +10.07 W above aifoundry2's law.
note: Laws refitted per card with the e-folding held at 36 C, rms 0.10 and 0.09 W.

statement: Idle during the 26 Sep catalogue: 32.8 W on aifoundry2 (die 67-92 C), 25.8 W on aifoundry3 (55-60 C), 34.3 W on aifoundry1-c1 (57-71 C).

Where idle goes at 73 C (aifoundry2): minions 11.05 W (35%), SRAM 2.00 W (6%), mesh 3.64 W (11%), no rail sensor (PCIe, DDR PHY, I/O shire, regulators) 15.10 W (48%); board 31.79 W. aifoundry1-c1 at 73 C: 15.96 / 3.05 / 5.83 / 17.87, board 42.71 W.

statement: The unsensed blocks move little with temperature (0.10 W/C on aifoundry2 over 74-88 C); the three metered rails carry the leakage, 0.53 W/C between them at 75-80 C.
note: aifoundry1-c1: 0.16 and 0.77 W/C.

statement: SRAM rail at idle (leakage of the L2/L3/scratchpad arrays): 1.60 W at 67 C, 2.63 W at 82 C on aifoundry2; slope 0.066 W/C on aifoundry3.
Dense fp32 matmul on random data at 80 C, priced from the tables: fixed 12.6 W + leakage 23.3 W + multiply-adds 26.5 W = 62.4 W, against 63.6 W measured: 57% of it is keeping the card on and leaking.
note: A decomposition checked against a measurement, not a prediction.

statement: The firmware's static TDP: 65 W on aifoundry2 and aifoundry1-c1, 0 W on aifoundry3 (set by a boot service), which pins aifoundry3 at 600 MHz; the driver reports 65 W on all.

statement: Governor thresholds in the firmware source: 65 C software and 65 W TDP (75 C / 75 W catastrophic), checked once per management pass (~133 ms on aifoundry2); no hysteresis; the power input is a PMIC measurement.
note: Read from et-platform source at 353f20e (thermal_pwr_mgmt.h); the cards run an older build.
page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

statement: 35 temperature sensors on the die (34 minion shires + the I/O shire, one per tile of the 6x6 grid except PCIe), 12-bit (0.061 C) in hardware; the host sees one 34-shire mean in whole degrees plus peak-hold extremes.
note: Firmware source (bl2_pvt_controller.h) and PRM sec. 1.6.

statement: At each rise, the hottest shire read 2-3 C above the chip mean (3-4 C in 61-83% of rises by card), but the host never learns which shire it was.
Idle die temperatures: aifoundry2 62-80 C (62 C after a night idle, 26.7 W; 80 C, 36.3 W), aifoundry3 near 50-56 C; under the catalogue the median busy die was 74 C (a2), 58 C (a3), 61 C (a1c1).
Under load the same work costs about 1 W more per C the die warms: 0.9-1.2 W/C at 73-97 C on aifoundry2 and aifoundry1-c1 (1.02 and 1.13 W/C in the load step), 0.6 W/C on the cooler aifoundry3.
Thermal resistance, card in its desktop box: 1.47 C/W total (six stages, 1.5 s to 2,500 s); leakage loop gain 0.95 at 80 C, passing 1 at 82 C: about 3 W of sustained switching power before runaway.
note: A fit (E17); do not apply to aifoundry3 (its heatsink is visibly faster).

statement: aifoundry3 under a back-to-back random-data heater: the die peaks at 90 C in 3 of 3 cycles (after 126-150 two-second bursts), against a predicted 60-66 C plateau.

statement: aifoundry1's card 0 overheats: ten minutes of short smoke blocks took its die to 98-102 C, and right after it read 115-117 C with nothing running, drawing 66-71 W at 600 MHz. It is excluded from all measurements.
Each mesh hop adds 12 cycles round trip at 600 MHz (20 ns): L3 11.99, remote scratchpad 12.00, TensorSend 12.01-12.02 cycles per hop on every card.
note: 20 ns at either clock (16 cycles at 800 MHz): a NoC-clock cost.

statement: One mesh hop is 3.72 mm of silicon (3.64-3.74; x 3.73, y 3.70), from Esperanto's die plot scaled to the 570 mm^2 die (25.6 x 22.2 mm).
note: An estimate from the die plot, not a measurement (05-claims kind A).

statement: A random bit per mm on free links, mesh rail at 0.485 V: 37 fJ (25 of it data-dependent); on board power 47 fJ. Dally's rule of thumb is ~100 fJ/b-mm.
note: Per card, mesh rail: a2 36.1, a3 35.8, a1c1 38.1 fJ; board 46.7, 44.4, 51.1 fJ (99% intervals in 05-claims). Scaled to 0.9 V the data cost is 85-105 fJ.

statement: On a busy mesh where flows share links the same random bit costs 53 fJ per mm on the mesh rail and 79 fJ on board power.

Per byte per hop, from the free-link figure: about 1.1 pJ/B on the mesh rail (37 fJ/bit-mm x 8 bits x 3.72 mm); the energy manual quotes Heat per millimetre as 1.5 pJ/B per hop on the mesh rail and 2.2 on board power for a loaded mesh.
source: derived from report.json headline x inputs.hop_mm; docs/energy-manual/05-bytes-between-cores.md:31

statement: Tensor loads from a scratchpad d hops away, fitted over 1-8 hops (board power): one hop costs 0.67 pJ/B on zeros [0.62-0.73] and 1.80 pJ/B on random data [1.72-1.91]; 142 fJ per random bit per hop is data-dependent.

statement: TensorSend across the mesh: 9.2 pJ/B to leave the shire plus 1.75 pJ/B per mean hop (three cards pooled; a2 9.1 + 1.8, a3 8.0 + 1.7, a1c1 10.4 + 1.7); no card's per-hop cost differs from another's.

statement: The ones carried cost energy, not only bits that flip: a stream of all ones costs 8-12% more per hop than random data on the mesh rail, though at one hop it costs 35-37% less.

statement: TensorSend round trip, 32 B register to register inside a shire: 68 cycles (113 ns) on the 7 fast-network tree edges of each neighbourhood, 114-115 cycles (190 ns) for every other pair.

statement: TensorSend round trip between shires, 32 B: 150 + 12.02 cycles per mesh hop (250 ns + 20 ns/hop), worst residual 1.1-1.4 cycles over all 496 shire pairs; 1 KB messages add 12 cycles per hop to 5 hops and 36 beyond.

statement: Credit-counter (FCC) round trip: 140.2 + 14.43 cycles per hop (234 ns + 24 ns/hop); blocking credit inside a shire 119.5-119.9 cycles (200 ns).

statement: A flag handed off through global atomics in memory (the GPU pattern): 610-1,150 ns round trip (median 873 ns across shires), with no measurable dependence on distance.

statement: Hardware allreduce (TensorReduce + TensorBroadcast) of 32 B over a shire's 32 minions: 444 cycles (0.74 us), 444.06-444.31 on all three cards.

statement: Hardware allreduce of 32 B over all 1,024 minions: 1,393 cycles (2.3 us), 1,392.6-1,393.4 on the three cards; an A100 grid.sync() alone is 1.1-1.2 us.

statement: One contended global atomic (amoaddg.w on one line, 1,024 minions): the bank retires one every 10.00 cycles, about 60 M/s for the whole chip; spread over 32 lines, one per shire, 0.31 cycles and 1,919 M/s: 32x.

statement: The host shire's own memory path stops, not slows: 384-392 of its loads get through per window (192-240 for a DRAM-backed line) whether the window is 5 ms or 100 ms, on every card.

statement: The switch is sharp: 21 remote requesters leave the host at 95.5-95.7% of its rate, 22 stop it (0.02%). Rule: the bank is not saturated while N x 10 cycles < P + t_round_trip (216 cycles).
